items.prompt: You have 2:40 left and no increment. White to move. What kind of position is this? (Decide how much of your remaining time it deserves.)

options: a tempting move loses a lot

claims.statement: White is in check.
White has exactly one legal move.

hints: Count White's legal moves.
Can anything capture the checking queen, or block, or can the king go anywhere else?
Only one square is available to the king.
items.explain: White has exactly one legal move, Kf1. A forced move deserves almost none of your clock; the time is better saved for the positions below.

items.prompt: You have 2:40 left and no increment. White to move. What kind of position is this?

options: a tempting move loses a lot

claims.statement: The engine's best move is one of three moves that are all within 40 centipawns of it.
No line wins more than a pawn for White.

hints: Look for a capture or a check that changes the material.
If you find none, ask how different the sensible moves really are.
Three different plans score within a fraction of a pawn.
items.explain: No forcing line wins material and three sensible moves are within 40 centipawns of each other. A long think here has little to find; a short think is enough.

items.prompt: You have 2:40 left and no increment. Black to move. What kind of position is this?

answer.class: a tempting move loses a lot
options: a tempting move loses a lot

claims.statement: The capture hxg5 is far worse than the best move.
The engine's best move is Qd8 or Qe7.

hints: Is there a capture that looks free?
Check what White can do after you take.
The pawn on g5 can be taken, and that capture is the costly mistake.
items.explain: The pawn capture hxg5 looks free but loses material by force, so one tempting move here is much worse than the sensible ones. This is the kind of moment to spend clock on.

items.prompt: You have 1:50 left and no increment. White to move. What kind of position is this?

answer.class: a tempting move loses a lot
options: a tempting move loses a lot

claims.statement: The capture Qxh5 is far worse than the best move.
dxe5 is the engine's best move.

hints: Is there a capture that looks free?
Check what Black can answer with a bishop move.
The knight on h5 can be taken; that capture is the costly mistake.
items.explain: Qxh5 wins a knight on the surface, but Bg4 traps the queen. A tempting capture with a hidden reply is the sign of a moment worth spending time on.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: Bxh4 is the engine's best move.
Nxc3 is clearly worse.

hints: Is any White piece loose?
Which of your pieces can capture it?
The bishop on e7 can take on h4.
items.explain: White's pawn move left the bishop on h4 loose, and Bxh4 takes it. A good decision here is one the engine agrees with, whatever happens later in the game.

items.prompt: A player took the b2 pawn with the queen here. The opponent then missed the best reply and the player won the game. Was Qxb2 a sound decision? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Qxb2 loses material along the engine's line.
Qxb2 is far worse than the best move.

hints: Set the result aside. Judge only the move.
What is White's best reply to Qxb2?
A knight move traps the queen.
items.explain: The engine rates Qxb2 far worse than the best move, because a knight move traps the queen. The game was won, but the decision was not sound. A win can hide a bad process, just as a loss can hide a good one.

items.prompt: A player castled queenside here (O-O-O) and later lost the game. Does the loss show that O-O-O was a mistake? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The engine's best move is O-O-O or c6, and both are within 40 centipawns of it.
No line wins more than a pawn for Black.

hints: Judge the move from this position only.
Does the engine find a clearly better move?
The best moves here score within a fraction of a pawn of each other.
items.explain: The engine rates O-O-O among the best moves, so the loss does not show it was a mistake. A loss is evidence about the whole game, not about every move in it.

items.prompt: After the game a player wrote: 'The knight on d4 attacks my queen on f3.' Is that an observation or a guess?

claims.statement: One Black piece attacks the queen on f3.
One White piece defends the queen on f3.

hints: Can you point to something on the board that settles it?
An observation can be checked by looking; a guess is a prediction or a judgment.
You can count the attackers on f3.
items.explain: It is an observation: you can point at the board and count. One Black piece (the knight) attacks f3, and one White piece (the g2 pawn) defends it.

items.prompt: Another note from the same game: 'My pawn on c2 is loose.' Observation or guess?

claims.statement: The pawn on c2 is White's only loose piece.

hints: Can the board answer this without any opinion?
Check whether the pawn is attacked and whether anything defends it.
It is a fact about attack and defence.
items.explain: It is an observation: the board shows the c2 pawn is attacked and nothing defends it. Observations like this are what you write down first.

items.prompt: A third note: 'I am lost.' Observation or guess? Then see what a test says.

claims.statement: The engine rates the position as close to level, not lost.

hints: Can you point at the board and settle it?
'Lost' is a judgment about the future.
The engine can test judgments of this kind.
items.explain: It is a guess, and a testable one: the engine rates the position as close to level. A feeling of being lost is data about you, not yet about the position.

items.prompt: A fourth note: 'Qd1 is my best move.' Observation or guess? Then see what a test says.

claims.statement: Qd1 is the engine's best move.
Qg3 is clearly worse.

hints: Is this something you can see, or something you judge?
A judgment can still be right.
It is a judgment; the engine agrees with it.
items.explain: It is a guess that happens to be right: the engine agrees that Qd1 is best. A guess that is confirmed by a test is worth more than one that is not.

items.prompt: White to move. A note says: 'Black is going to win my e4 pawn.' Observation or guess?

claims.statement: The pawn on e4 is attacked once.
The pawn on e4 is defended twice.
The engine rates the position as roughly level.

hints: Separate what you can count from what you predict.
Attackers and defenders are facts; 'is going to win' is a forecast.
The forecast is the guess.
items.explain: The attack and defence counts are observations (one attacker, two defenders); 'is going to win' is a guess about the future, and the engine does not support it.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: Qxd7 is checkmate.

hints: Look at the checks first.
Is there a capture that ends the game?
The queen takes on d7.
items.explain: Qxd7 is checkmate. A high confidence is easy to justify when the answer is a mate you can verify move by move.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: exd5 is the engine's best move.
cxd5 is far worse.

hints: Two recaptures are possible. Which one feels natural?
After the natural one, what can White play?
Retake with the other pawn.
items.explain: The natural pawn recapture cxd5 loses material to a knight move; exd5 is the engine's choice. This is a case where feeling sure and being right come apart.

items.prompt: Black to move. Does Black have a forcing move that wins material? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: No line wins more than a pawn for Black.
The engine rates the position as roughly level.

hints: List the checks, then the captures.
Does any of them gain material?
None does; the position is quiet.
items.explain: No forcing line wins material and the position is level. Here 'low' or 'medium' confidence in a quiet claim is honest, and it is fine to say so.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: exd4 is the engine's best move.
Bxc3 is far worse.

hints: Two captures are on the board. Picture the position after each.
One capture takes the queen outright.
Take the queen with the pawn.
items.explain: exd4 takes White's queen; Bxc3 also takes a piece and is far worse. Note whether your confidence matched how hard the choice really was.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: Qa5+ is the engine's best move.
Qa5+ wins material along the engine's line.

hints: Your checks first.
Does a queen check also attack something?
The queen checks from a5.
items.explain: Qa5+ attacks the king and the bishop on b5 at once, so Black wins a piece. A fork you can verify is a good place for high confidence.

items.prompt: A player's note: 'I played Nxe4, taking the pawn at once. I never looked at what Black could do with a check.' The move loses material. Which kind of error does the note describe? (A tentative label: only the player knows.)

claims.statement: Nxe4 is far worse than the best move.

hints: Does the note say the player saw the refutation?
'Never looked' points to the first of the four boxes.
The reply was not seen at all.
items.explain: The note says the reply was never looked at, so the tentative label is 'not seen'. The engine confirms Nxe4 is a real mistake; the note says why it happened.

items.prompt: A player's note: 'I saw White's knight check on c6. I counted the trades after it and thought I came out fine, but my count was wrong.' The move Nxa4 loses material. Which kind of error does the note describe?

claims.statement: Nxa4 is far worse than the best move.

hints: Did the player see the key reply?
The reply was seen, so the box is not 'not seen'.
The player calculated and got the result wrong.
items.explain: The reply was seen, the calculation was done, and the result was wrong. That is 'seen but miscalculated', which asks for a different practice from 'not seen'.

items.prompt: A player's note: 'I counted cxd4 to the end and it did win a pawn. I thought the position afterwards was good for me. It was not.' Which kind of error does the note describe?

claims.statement: cxd4 wins a pawn along the engine's line.
cxd4 is far worse than the best move.
Rag1 is the engine's best move.

hints: Was the calculation wrong in this note?
The calculation was right: material was won.
The error was in judging the position afterwards.
items.explain: The count was right (a pawn is won), but the engine rates the resulting position far below the best move. The error was in the judgment, not in the calculation.

items.prompt: A player's note: 'I had nine seconds left and took the first capture I saw.' The move Bxc5 loses material. Which kind of error does the note describe?

claims.statement: Bxc5 is far worse than the best move.

hints: What does the note say about the clock?
A rushed first-capture move points to the clock.
The time left is the stated cause.
items.explain: The note blames the clock and a rushed first move. The tentative label is 'time pressure'. A later check of the clock times in the error log can confirm or refute it.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: dxc4 is the engine's best move.
b5 is far worse.

hints: What did Black's last move do?
Check what you can take back.
Retake on c4.
items.explain: Black's bishop took the bishop on c4 and the pawn on d3 can retake; the engine's other tries are far worse. This item is the baseline: your first answer, before practice.

items.prompt: White to move. Black's last move took a piece. Find the best recapture.

claims.statement: Bxc3 is the engine's best move.
f5 is far worse.

hints: What did Black's last move capture?
Which of your pieces can retake?
Retake with the bishop.
items.explain: Black's bishop took on c3 and the bishop on d2 retakes. This is the practice position: the same skill as the baseline, in a different position.

items.prompt: This position is the practice position flipped left to right. Would remembering your practice answer be enough to solve it? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The mirrored move is the engine's best move.

hints: Compare this board with the practice board.
Flip the practice answer left to right.
The mirrored move is the answer.
items.explain: The mirrored move is best here, so memory of the practice answer would pass this check without testing the skill. A good check uses a position from a different family.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: a7 is the engine's best move.
Qd1 is far worse.

hints: Which of your pieces is attacked?
Running away is not the only answer.
Advance the pawn.
items.explain: The a6 pawn was attacked; advancing it to a7 is the engine's choice and the retreats are far worse. This is the later check: a new position of the same skill, not seen in practice.
